# Discussion

This study derived functional player roles for nine EuroLeague seasons from open data and found that five roles — ball handler, wing, stretch forward, interior forward and rim protector — were reproducible under resampling and across periods, whereas finer partitions were not. The roles overlapped with registered positions at the two ends of the positional spectrum but cut across positions in between, and the role composition of a lineup did not explain its performance once the individual quality of its players was taken into account.

The roles correspond to those most often reported in the literature: the systematic review by Coma Ribes et al. lists floor generals, shooters, versatile players and paint protectors among its recurrent roles [@ribes2026identifying], and studies using play-type data distinguish ball handlers, spot-up wings and several types of bigs [@chen2023modeling; @wei2025enhancing]. The number of roles reported elsewhere ranges widely, from three in the women's EuroLeague [@pendolareinecke2025exploring] to nine [@ibanez2025redefining] and more than a dozen with play-type data [@chen2023modeling; @wei2025enhancing]. Our results suggest that, with box-score, shot-location and assist-network information, partitions finer than five roles are not stable; the instability of a seven-cluster solution on the same data illustrates that internal validity indices alone do not guarantee a reproducible partition. Finer distinctions may require play-type or tracking information that was not available here.

The claim that modern basketball is "positionless" was only partly supported. Ball handlers and rim protectors remained tied to the guard and centre positions, whereas wings and forwards were functionally interchangeable across registered positions. Positionless play in the EuroLeague therefore appears to be a property of the middle of the positional spectrum rather than of the game as a whole.

Role composition did not improve the prediction of lineup net rating beyond RAPM, with either five or four roles. Earlier links between roles and success were established without adjusting for the quality of the players involved: lineup net rating was modelled from soft cluster memberships alone and was not validated out of sample [@kalman2020lineup], semi-final qualification was regressed on team role counts without player efficiency or playing time [@chen2023modeling], and role proportions were derived from players selected on high plus-minus [@penner2025player]. Our sensitivity analysis shows how apparent role effects can also arise from lineup selection itself: when very short lineups are included, lineups that concede runs are substituted quickly and enter the analysis with strongly negative net ratings, and selecting "significant" combinations followed by a chi-square test then indicates a non-random role distribution that disappears under a permutation test and a minimum-duration filter. The practical implication is that a good lineup is, to a first approximation, a lineup of good players. This does not exclude small synergy effects, which the noise in segment-level outcomes would make hard to detect.

The box-score valuation index was strongly role-dependent, favouring rim protectors and interior forwards, whereas RAPM was not, and RAPM predicted future lineup outcomes considerably better. Indices of this type should therefore not be used to compare players across roles.

## Limitations

Segment-level net rating is very noisy, and all models explained little variance in absolute terms; small synergy effects may therefore have gone undetected. The permutation test carries the same noise as the observed data, so the comparison is fair, but the result should be read as an absence of evidence that role mix adds to player quality rather than as evidence of no effect. Only pairwise role interactions were tested, because higher-order combinations cannot be estimated reliably in samples of this size; play-type data would allow such tests in future work. Defensive behaviour was represented indirectly by steals, blocks, rebounds and fouls, yet the same role structure emerged with each group of variables, which suggests that the roles are not an artefact of the offensive emphasis of the data. The wing role was only moderately stable and should be used descriptively; the main conclusion about role composition did not change with the four-role solution, in which wings are absorbed into neighbouring roles. Role labels were derived from full-season statistics, but these do not include lineup outcomes, and the predictive test was carried out out of time. The findings are specific to the EuroLeague, but because data and code are open the analysis can be repeated directly in other leagues.

## Conclusions

Five functional roles describe EuroLeague players reproducibly from open data and remain tied to registered positions only at the guard and centre extremes. Because role mix adds little to lineup performance beyond the quality of the players involved, teams can use these roles to describe and scout players while valuing them, and building lineups, with plus-minus-based measures rather than with role combinations or box-score valuation indices.
